reasoning_summary: Counterexample-first audit of the riskiest concrete claims found nothing refutable. Necessary direction (both proofs): naturality of alpha : F -> G on C x D instantiated at the morphisms (f, id_D) and (id_C, g) of the product category gives exactly the two squares G(f,id_D) . alpha_(C,D) = alpha_(C',D) . F(f,id_D) and G(id_C,g) . alpha_(C,D) = alpha_(C,D') . F(id_C,g), which are by definition the naturality squares for alpha(-,D) and alpha(C,-), since F(-,D)f = F(f,id_D) and F(C,-)g = F(id_C,g). Sufficient direction: the load-bearing decomposition (id_C', g) . (f, id_D) = (id_C' . f, g . id_D) = (f, g) holds in the product category (componentwise composition plus identity laws), so bifunctoriality gives G(f,g) = G(id_C',g) . G(f,id_D) and F(f,g) = F(id_C',g) . F(f,id_D); pasting the horizontal square at D (from (2)) with the vertical square at C' (from (1), instantiated at the object C', which is legitimate since (1) is assumed for every object of C) yields G(f,g) . alpha_(C,D) = alpha_(C',D') . F(f,g). I tried to break this by seeking a structure where separate naturality in each variable fails to give joint naturality, but the pasting argument uses only the product-category composition law and functoriality of F and G, both of which hold by definition, so no counterexample exists. Remaining defects are transcription typos that are not relied upon: line 0041 labels the bottom arrow F(-,D)f instead of G(-,D)f; line 0181 writes G(C,-)f instead of G(C,-)g; line 0218 writes G(f,id_D) instead of F(f,id_D) on the right-hand side of (3). The subsequent uses (line 0236-0237) invoke the correct form of (3), which is exactly what line 0213 states, so the mathematical content of every inference is sound.
